idea_name: Activity-driven tick bars vs clock time bars as information-intensity sampler
mechanism: Build OHLC from tick streams by fixed tick count (median ticks per M5/M15/M30 → tick-200/500/1000 on EURUSD 2023–2024) timestamped at bar end+1µs; time bars oversample quiet hours and undersample active hours, while tick bars complete only after a preset activity volume so features align with real-time information arrival.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD ticks 2023–2024; compared to M5/M15/M30 time bars; tick-200 ≈ M5 activity
why_new_for_mis: Turns market activity intensity into the sampling clock itself—MIS can treat bar arrival rate / tick density as a continuous liquidity-and-information sensor rather than assuming uniform clock bars.
quote: time bars oversample information during low-activity periods and undersample information during high-activity periods… Activity-driven bars… complete only after a predetermined volume of market activity

idea_name: Bar absolute-return concentration: fraction of bars explaining total price change
mechanism: plot_volatility_analysis_of_bars ranks |close/open−1|; for each threshold bin plots proportion of candles to the right vs proportion of total absolute price change they produce—shows ~20% of M5 time-bars explain ~51% of move vs ~46% for tick-200, with tick-bar |ΔP| histograms monotonically decreasing.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a sampling-quality / vol-concentration diagnostic: whether a few bars dominate realized move mass—useful as a regime check on how information is packed in the chosen bar family.
quote: approximately 20% of time-bars explain roughly 51% of the total price change, whereas 20% of tick-bars explain roughly 46% of the total price change

idea_name: Trend-scanning: data-adaptive horizon via max |t-stat| of linear trend
mechanism: For each event, OLS slopes over multiple forward (or backward) windows in span (e.g. 5–99); select horizon maximizing |t-value|; bin=sign(t); also emit slope, R², ret, chosen window—horizons shorten in choppy markets and lengthen in persistent trends without a fixed forecast horizon.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5; MA20/50 crossover events; train 2018–2021, OOS 2021–2024; span=(5,100)
why_new_for_mis: Senses regime-dependent prediction horizon and trend significance as a continuous change sensor (t_value, window) rather than a fixed-bar label—MIS can watch optimal-horizon shifts as a market-dynamics feature.
quote: Instead of arbitrarily choosing to predict 5 or 10 days ahead, trend-scanning dynamically determines the most statistically significant horizon for each market condition.

idea_name: Expanding-quantile volatility mask on trend-scan windows
mechanism: Rolling std of log-prices over max horizon; expanding quantile at volatility_threshold (e.g. 0.05–0.3) defines a dynamic floor; windows below the floor zero-mask t-value/slope/R² so low-activity regimes cannot emit spurious trend labels.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5 trend-scan meta-labels; thresholds 0.0–0.3 tabulated
why_new_for_mis: Couples trend sensing to a self-updating low-vol gate—MIS can reuse expanding vol quantiles as a soft ‘noise regime’ veto independent of the labeling use case.
quote: This prevents the algorithm from generating spurious signals during low-activity periods when price movements are primarily noise. By using expanding quantiles, the threshold adapts to changing market volatility regimes.

mechanism: Joblib/time-aware cache keys, data-access contamination tracker, CV/backtest cache decorators—engineering for research velocity with no new market regime/vol/liquidity/sequence sensor constructed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic financial ML pipeline; EURUSD examples referenced from prior parts

quote: This article shows you how to eliminate this bottleneck using intelligent caching.

mechanism: Pruner sets volatility_tolerance = 0.1*(1+CV(events['w'])); high return-weight CV (trending / large-move regimes) widens allowed fold-score swings before prune; low CV (mean-reverting) tightens; plus entropy baseline from return-weighted label probs and n_warmup_steps=2 across regime-break folds.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD triple-barrier examples; GBPJPY weekly trending example; CV spanning 2019–2022 COVID fold
why_new_for_mis: Treats cross-fold score instability as a regime-heterogeneity sensor and scales pruning tolerance by economic-weight dispersion—MIS can monitor weight CV and fold-score std as live regime-break flags during model search.
quote: The volatility tolerance is proportional to the coefficient of variation of the return-attribution weights: trending markets (high CV) receive a wider tolerance; mean-reverting markets (low CV) receive a tighter one.

idea_name: Purged-CV fold score_std as regime-sensitivity overfitting flag
mechanism: check_for_overfitting callback warns when std of fold scores >0.3; high score_std across purged splits indicates the model captures regime-specific patterns rather than generalizable signal.
data_needed: per-fold neg_log_loss or f1 under PurgedKFold
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Financial HPO studies with 5-fold purged CV on triple-barrier / trend-scan labels
why_new_for_mis: Turns validation dispersion itself into a regime-change / non-stationarity sensor for MIS model health, separate from mean CV score.
quote: A high score_std across a 5-fold purged split often indicates a model capturing regime-specific patterns rather than genuinely generalizable signal

idea_name: BidAskLongShortPipeline: side-specific execution-price edge vs spread
mechanism: Train separate primary/secondary pipelines on ask bars (longs) and bid bars (shorts); report spread_mean/spread_bps and per-side CV scores—if short CV collapses relative to long, bid–ask spread is consuming short-side edge.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX-style MT5 symbols in Blueprint pipeline (symbol configurable)
why_new_for_mis: Makes spread asymmetry a first-class liquidity sensor that can veto one side of the book when microstructure cost kills that direction’s measurable edge.
quote: If the short model's CV score falls materially below the long model's, the bid-ask spread is consuming the short-side edge and that direction should not be traded at current spread levels.

mechanism: At each timestamp average get_signal sizes over all bets still open (t1 not expired); Numba-parallel; converts overlapping triple-barrier concurrency into a bounded ±1 portfolio exposure series that spikes when signal density is high.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any classifier strategy with overlapping triple-barrier labels (AFML Ch.10 toolkit)
why_new_for_mis: Concurrency count / averaged active signal is a real-time density-of-opportunity sensor MIS can use as a liquidity-stress or crowding proxy when many barriers remain open.
quote: during a period of unusually dense signal generation, fifteen or twenty signals may activate in quick succession… total exposure reaches 150–200% of capital

idea_name: bet_size_reserve: EF3M two-Gaussian CDF on concurrent long−short imbalance
mechanism: Fit mixture of two Gaussians to c_t=active_long−active_short via EF3M (first 5 moments); map CDF conditional on sign of c_t to bet size in [−1,1]—captures bimodal neutral/transition vs strong-directional position regimes without requiring classifier probabilities.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Trend-following / directional strategies with concurrent longs and shorts; generic AFML bet_sizing
why_new_for_mis: Learns an empirical regime fingerprint of the strategy’s own position book (neutral vs directional modes) that MIS can treat as a data-driven market-state / crowding sensor.
quote: There are many observations where longs and shorts roughly cancel… clustering near zero. And there are many observations where the strategy has taken a strong directional view… A mixture of two Gaussians… captures the bimodality

idea_name: CPCV path-fan width as model+sizer fragility sensor
mechanism: For each of φ[N,k] combinatorial purged paths, simulate fresh PropFirmAccountState bar-by-bar with path-specific OOF probs; distribution_report and equity-fan plots measure terminal-equity dispersion, daily/overall limit breach rates, and PBO—wide fans = path-dependent fragility.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Prop-firm-style accounts (FundedNext Stellar 2-Step example); φ paths illustrated with 20 curves
why_new_for_mis: Pathwise Sharpe/equity dispersion under CPCV is a structural robustness sensor MIS can attach to any dynamically sized strategy, beyond a single backtest Sharpe.
quote: The width of the fan is the visual signature of fragility—a tight fan indicates performance robust to the data partition, while a wide fan reveals that a single historical backtest could be drawn from anywhere in that spread.

idea_name: OOF isotonic calibration + MCE high-confidence tail as overconfidence sensor
mechanism: CalibratorCV fits isotonic (or Platt) map on PurgedKFold OOF probs; monitor Brier/ECE/MCE—MCE flags worst bin, typically the 0.75–0.90 tail where RF overstates win rates; re-fit after regime shifts; reliability diagram with bootstrap CI.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Financial ML classifiers (RF/GBM) feeding bet_size_probability / Kelly; pipeline calibrate=True
why_new_for_mis: Quantifies probability-scale distortion as a sensing channel: MIS can treat ECE/MCE and reliability-curve gap as confidence-quality sensors that gate sizing after regime changes.
quote: In financial applications, the worst-performing probability region is usually the high-confidence tail, where the model assigns 0.75–0.90 but delivers win rates of 0.58–0.65.

idea_name: Session-stratified hourly spread distribution as liquidity cost sensor
mechanism: MQL5 TransactionCostCollector CopySpread + CopyTime → mean spread pips per broker hour 0–23; Python session_adjusted_spread_pips(hour) and p95_pips feed TransactionCostModel—London–NY overlap tightest, off-session hours systematically wider than mean.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD illustrated; any MT5 symbol via collector script; holding_days 0 vs 2 for intraday vs swing
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a broker-measured, hour-resolved liquidity friction surface—usable as a session liquidity regime feature and as a cost gate independent of mid-price vol.
quote: The London–New York overlap (hours 12–17) shows the tightest spreads; hours outside active sessions show substantially wider spreads that a mean-based cost estimate would systematically understate.

idea_name: O-U φ/half-life and forecast case as post-entry process regime
mechanism: OLS on discrete O-U from cost-adjusted trade P&L estimates φ (half-life) and residual σ; forecast∈{0, E[P&L], E[win]} encodes mean-reversion vs directional belief; OTR mesh over 100k synthetic paths picks PT/SL—process parameters characterize how price behaves after entry.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 RSI example; ATR-based initial barriers; prop-firm $25k / 0.5 lot / 2 concurrent → 125 pip SL cap
why_new_for_mis: Half-life and forecast case are explicit sensors of mean-reverting vs trending post-entry dynamics—MIS can track φ/hl drift as a regime label for exit-rule suitability.
quote: The forecast parameter is what distinguishes these three cases… Choosing between them requires stating clearly which variant the trading rule is being calibrated for.

idea_name: Four bagging draw regimes: between-tree ρ and uniqueness as concurrency sensors
mechanism: Compare A full uniform bootstrap, B uniform at max_samples=avg uniqueness, C sequential at avgU, D sequential at 1.0 on identical DecisionTree bags; measure draw-uniqueness ratio and mean pairwise OOB-prob correlation ρ—on EURUSD tick/tick-imb/M5, A→B (count throttle) drives decorrelation; B→C sequential rule adds little; D worst.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD 2022–2023; ~1269–1289 meta-events on tick bars (avgU≈0.435); M5 replication 11,833 events (avgU≈0.462)
why_new_for_mis: Makes label-concurrency regime observable via ensemble ρ and uniqueness ratios, and shows draw-count (not sequential rule) is the operative lever—MIS can monitor avg uniqueness and bagging ρ as redundancy/regime-quality sensors.
quote: the lever that moves the §6.2 covariance term is the draw count, not the draw rule… set max_samples to average uniqueness with an ordinary bootstrap
